newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN GOVT TO KEEP EYE ON MTN, TRANSNET TALKS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN GOVT TO KEEP EYE ON MTN, TRANSNET TALKS.

text.p: South Africa's Transnet is in talks on a deal with phones group Mobile Telephones Network (MTN) but a government spokesman said on Thursday any deal will be vetted by the ministries of Telecommunications and Public Enterprises.
MTN's communications director Jacques Sellschop told Reuters MTN was interested in striking a deal to acquire the subscriber database of state-owned Transnet's phone operation Transtel Cellular.
The buyer would be MTN's M-Tel associate company.
"MTN has been having talks with its 20 percent shareholder and exclusive service provider Transtel about the prospect of taking over Transtel's subscriber database," he said.
But Sellschop added that no agreement had been sealed. "However, at this stage nothing has yet been finalised," he said.

But confusion surrounds the scale of the deal as Business Day newspaper, citing confidential company documents, reported on Wednesday that MTN is negotiating for the purchase of the entire cellular unit.

Sellschop declined to comment on whether MTN was interested in eventually buying the whole division, but industry sources said such a move could be a logical outcome of buying the database even if it were not the subject of current talks.
Another area of confusion has been the role the government may play in any planned deal.
Wandile Zote, a spokesman for the Ministry of Public Enterprises, said on Thursday that any deal would have to be vetted by that ministry and also the Telecommunications ministry.

The ministries see any deal involving Transtel as coming under the aegis of the National Framework Agreement (NFA) -- whereby government, labour unions and business have agreed to discuss any restructuring of state-owned assets.
"This is a restructuring issue...the minister for Telecommunications and the minister for Public Enterprises have to be informed of the process before any decision can be taken," Zote said.
Local media has reported that Stella Sigcau, the Public Enterprises Minister, has already blocked the deal between MTN and Transtel.
But Zote said this was untrue. No decision had been made and the government was just seeking to inform both parties of their commitments under the NFA.
"All the minister is saying is that if you have any plans to sell Cellular, or a part of it, to MTN then this is the procedure you need to follow," he said.
Sellschop said it was up to Transtel -- as a state-owned asset -- to be aware of any NFA implications.

"MTN at no time felt uncomfortable or felt that it was contravening the protocols of the NFA by discussing a deal of this nature. It is the prerogative of Transtel, the seller, to determine any NFA implications," he said.
